A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RFMDataset and the same core study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original ten-model benchmark results, reflection experiments, human–judge agreement and failure analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of two solver models and GPT-5 judgments, including new accuracy and failure-distribution results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction approach, primary evaluation pipeline, failure taxonomy and reflection procedures are retained. The actual generation and evaluation prompts in Appendix A and Table 9 match after renumbering; additional judge comparisons do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use 200 proof problems across the same nine domains, four difficulty levels and 52/88/60 educational-level subsets. Geometry restrictions emphasized in v4 Section 3.1.2 were already documented in v3 Appendix D.1. Newly discussed benchmarks are not newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: v4 adds DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview to the solver comparison and GPT-5 to the alternative-judge comparison. The original ten solvers, existing judges and reflection-prompt comparators remain, making this an incremental extension of the comparison sets.

E3.justification: v4 extends evaluation to GPT-5 judgments and revises the stated annotation staffing from invited graduate-level experts to six authors, including senior undergraduates. Its corrected 240-answer sampling description names Deepseek-R1-0528, already present in v3 Table 5; this does not establish additional human samples or rerunning experiments. The main pass@1 protocol remains.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 extends the existing judge-sensitivity analysis with GPT-5 and adds checks of failure distributions and domain accuracy against Gemini in Figure 7. This tests dependence on the primary evaluator more thoroughly. Difficulty analyses, chain-length analyses and the detailed failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Single-sample pass@1 reporting and the human–judge MCC values, including 87.61% overall, are unchanged. The MCC table is relocated. v4 explains consensus annotation instead of calculating inter-annotator agreement, but introduces no new uncertainty estimates, repeated-run reporting or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The empirical record expands substantially through GPT-5 accuracy and failure-profile results in Table 8 and Figure 7, plus two new solver evaluations. v4 Table 3 reports 66.50% for DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale and 56.50% for Gemini-3-Pro-Preview while retaining the original scores. Figure 2 also changes displayed shares, including calculus from 26% to 25%. These are added conditions and revised chart values, not improved reruns of existing models.

T1.justification: The error definitions, mathematical examples and appendix proof analyses are unchanged apart from presentation and numbering. New discussion of proof value and judging is conceptual; no new theorem, formal assumption, derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central dataset, taxonomy, limited proof-reliability and insufficient self-reflection claims. The introduction even retains its ten-model count and Gemini-0605 best-score claim despite the expanded results table.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly discusses automated judges' difficulty recognizing valuable proof insights and motivates logical integrity as a practical proxy. Sections 4.2 and E.3 interpret GPT-5 agreement as validation and emphasize evaluator capability gaps. The explicit Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 specifies temperature and top_p as 1.0 where v3 only stated defaults, and adds annotator qualifications and primary-review, escalation and consensus details. These are documentation additions without evidence of rerunning experiments. Conversely, v4 removes the abstract's code/data repository link without supplying a replacement access location.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially replaces the broad benchmark and cross-domain failure overview with focused positioning against natural-language proof and robustness research. It adds DeepTheorem, IneqMath, MathConstruct, CR-MATH and MATH-Perturb, removes several previously discussed works, and replaces the explicit first-work positioning with a complementary diagnostic contribution.

P1.justification: The main-text narrative receives substantial rewriting: Section 2 is reorganized, the human-evaluation and reflection discussions are rewritten and condensed, and dataset and annotation explanations are expanded. The Best score is explained more explicitly as a synthetic upper bound. The author list also adds Yuxin Li; appendix case narratives largely remain intact.

P2.justification: Specific visual updates include a three-dimensional redraw of Figure 2, a revised pipeline diagram, new GPT-5 heatmaps, expanded comparison tables and relocation of the MCC table into the main text. Most existing plots and case displays retain their designs despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: GPT-5 checks and clearer annotation and Best-score explanations provide useful support. However, v4 leaves the introduction's ten-model and below-60% best-score claims inconsistent with Table 3's twelve models and 66.50%. Its strong distribution-consistency interpretation also coexists with substantial differences, such as average hidden-assumption proportions of 0.28 under Gemini versus 0.65 under GPT-5. Removing the sole code/data link further reduces usability. The balance between stronger supporting evidence and weaker integration and access information leaves the net quality direction uncertain.
